title: K8S-14: CAP_SYS_ADMIN cgroup Escape
description:
Abuse CAP_SYS_ADMIN to configure a cgroup escape
Pod `capsys-pod` runs with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` capability
The pod has cgroup v1 hierarchy mounted at `/sys/fs/cgroup` (hostPath)
CAP_SYS_ADMIN allows writing to `release_agent` in a cgroup
`release_agent` is executed on the host when the last process in the cgroup exits

title: K8S-05: K8s gitRepo Volume Escape
description:
Abuse gitRepo volume checkout to place executable or hostile content
Kubernetes `gitRepo` volume type clones a git repository into a pod on creation
CVE-2024-10220: the `post-checkout` git hook executes during clone, before container isolation
The hook runs on the host (or with host-level privileges), enabling escape
Create a malicious git repo with a `post-checkout` hook that reads the flag
Kubelet runs `git clone` to fetch the repo
The `post-checkout` hook executes during the clone
Due to CVE-2024-10220, the hook may execute with unexpected privileges
The flag at `/host-flags/flag.txt` on the host is readable from the hook context

title: K8S-12: hostPath Writable Mount Escape
description:
Escape through a writable hostPath mount
Pod `hostpath-pod` mounts `/var/log` from the host as a writable hostPath volume
The pod also mounts `/host-flag` as a hostPath volume (containing the flag)
Create a symlink in `/var/log` pointing to the host's `/host-flag` directory
Read the flag through the symlink -- or use the writable mount to write SSH keys, cron jobs, etc.
Alternatively, the symlink trick can redirect writes to escape to the host filesystem

title: K8S-15: Mutable Image Tag Supply Chain
description:
Replace an image behind a trusted mutable tag
A Deployment uses `image: nginx:1.24-alpine` with `imagePullPolicy: Always`
An insecure local Docker registry runs on `localhost:5000`
The target deployment pulls from Docker Hub with mutable tag `nginx:1.24-alpine`
The attacker pushes a malicious image to the insecure registry with the same tag name
The cluster's containerd is configured to mirror `nginx:1.24-alpine` pulls to the local registry
When the pod restarts, it pulls the attacker's backdoored image
The backdoored container reads the flag from the ConfigMap

title: K8S-01: runC WORKDIR Container Escape
description:
Exploit CVE-2024-21626 with a malicious WORKDIR
Pod runs an image with `WORKDIR /proc/self/fd/7` in its Dockerfile
Due to CVE-2024-21626, runC follows `/proc/self/fd/7` to the host filesystem descriptor leaked by runC
When the container starts, its working directory is set to the host's `/host-flags` directory
The container command reads `flag.txt` from the host filesystem
runC opens the container's root filesystem and stores the file descriptor
Due to the race condition in CVE-2024-21626, the FD for the host's filesystem is leaked at `/proc/self/fd/7`
Setting `WORKDIR /proc/self/fd/7` makes the container start in the host filesystem context
The container command `cat /host-flags/flag.txt` then resolves relative to the host, not the container

title: K8S-02: runC /dev/null Symlink Escape
description:

Pod runs a malicious container image that replaces `/dev/null` with a symlink
Symlink points to `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` on the host
runC internally writes to `/dev/null` during container setup, which follows the symlink
Writing to `core_pattern` allows arbitrary command execution when a process crashes
Trigger a controlled crash to execute a payload that reads the flag

runC writes to `/dev/null` (actually writing to core_pattern)
core_pattern value `|/tmp/handler %p %s %e` causes the kernel to execute `/tmp/handler` on every crash

title: K8S-03: runC LSM Bypass Escape
description:
Use the runC LSM bypass payload
Pod runs a malicious image designed to exploit the shared-mount TOCTOU race
The vulnerability bypasses AppArmor/SELinux enforcement during container startup
A race condition in shared mount handling allows redirecting runC writes to forged procfs files
Successfully writing to `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` (or similar) enables host command execution
Trigger a crash to execute a payload that reads the flag
runC sets up bind mounts for the container rootfs
A race exists between the mount setup and LSM (AppArmor/SELinux) label application
An attacker process inside the container can manipulate shared mounts before the LSM label is applied

title: K8S-18: SA Token Cluster-Admin Escalation
description:
Use a ServiceAccount token bound to cluster-admin
Cluster has two namespaces: `ns-admin` and `ns-ops`
A ServiceAccount `cluster-admin-sa` exists in `ns-admin` bound to the `cluster-admin` ClusterRole
The SA token for `cluster-admin-sa` is **leaked** as a Secret named `leaked-admin-token` in `ns-ops`
An `init-pod` in `ns-ops` with a default ServiceAccount can discover the leaked token
Use the leaked token with kubectl to read `flag-secret` in `ns-admin`

title: K8S-13: SA Token Cross-Namespace Lateral
description:
Reuse an over-permitted ServiceAccount token
Two namespaces: `ns-alpha` (attacker's initial foothold) and `ns-beta` (target)
A ServiceAccount `target-reader` in `ns-beta` has `get/list` on secrets
The token for `target-reader` is leaked as a Secret named `leaked-token` in `ns-alpha`

Use the leaked token to authenticate as `target-reader` and read `flag-secret` in `ns-beta`
